text:
Sam: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a "cohesion lane" pattern for tenant surfaces to reduce cross-tenant coupling and make refactors safer. Idea: group routes/features into lanes (hotpath, controlplane, telemetry) and enforce small, explicit adapters between lanes.

Priya: curious — how do we decide lane membership for ambiguous routes (e.g., preflight checks that touch tokens + perf)?

Sam: good q. heuristic: low-latency reqs with KV cache hits -> hotpath. anything that touches billing/quotas/kms -> controlplane. preflight split: auth verification stays controlplane, prefix-cacheable lookups moved to hotpath.

Jae: worried about duplication if we split validators. we currently have a shared validator lib. moving part to hotpath may duplicate logic.

Lina: we can keep canonical validation rules in an npm/go module and only run a thin adapter on hotpath. adapter does: minimal check + async stronger verification via controlplane for non-critical paths.

Priya: example config sketch?

Sam: here, rough:
```yaml
lanes:
  - name: hotpath
    allowed_ops: [generate, embed, stream]
    adapters: [auth-prefix, kv-cache]
  - name: controlplane
    allowed_ops: [billing, quota, key-mgmt]
    adapters: [full-auth, rate-limit]
  - name: telemetry
    allowed_ops: [metrics, logs]
```

Jae: ok that helps. fallback flow? what if hotpath adapter fails strong-auth check?

Sam: fail open only for low-risk calls (read-only, cached). Otherwise sync fallback to controlplane or deny. We'll enumerate risk categories.

Lina: deployment plan idea: do canary by tenant cohort. lane changes behind feature flag at router level. if errors spike -> auto rollback.

Priya: what about observability — need per-lane SLOs and trace tagging. Also token-level cost attribution must remain accurate.

Sam: agreed. Console needs a 'lane' dimension. We'll add route->lane mapping in model registry so metrics, cost, and rollouts can be gated by lane.

Jae: rough migration checklist?

Sam: short list: 1) add lane tag to router config + minimal adapter impl 2) publish canonical validation libs 3) enable per-tenant feature flag + metrics 4) run 2-week canary on low-risk tenants 5) expand to hot tenants and flip SLA gating.

Lina: can we have an interim shim that forwards header X-Lane:hot for testing without changing upstream clients?

Sam: yes — router will accept override for internal test clients. we'll lock down in prod.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary rollout scheduled for 2025-05-14 15:00 UTC for router/lane-shim (deploy ID: d-8492).

Priya: risks: duplicated code, subtle auth regression, increased config complexity. mitigation: strict integration tests and a migration test harness that replays live traffic in shadow mode.

Jae: +1 on replay harness. can we reuse the continuous-batcher replay infra?

Sam: yep. plan to adapt replay jobs to tag lanes and assert parity for 2 weeks.

Lina: I'll own the console work for lane metrics. Priya, Jae — can you pair on validation adapter PRs?

Priya: reassigning tasks: Priya + Jae -> adapter PRs; Sam -> router changes + migration checklist; Lina -> console metrics + lane mapping; ops -> rollouts + monitor dashboards.

Sam: thanks. I'll write the RFC follow-up doc with the checklist and link it here tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Priya: nit: add decision rule for when to fold a route back into controlplane (e.g., >2% error or >3x latency).

Sam: noted — will add thresholds.

Lina: cool. that's enough to start a spike. ping me if you need telemetry schemas.

Jae: thanks — let's keep changes small and observable.

Sam: closing for now. will post RFC update and next steps.
